title: Lists
lesson:
A **list** keeps many values in order: `kg = [40, 12, 55]`. Indexing and slicing work like strings (`kg[0]` is 40, `kg[-1]` is 55), but lists can **change**:
- `kg.append(30)` adds to the end; `kg.insert(0, 5)` adds at a position
- `kg.remove(12)` removes that value; `kg.pop()` removes and gives back the last one
- `kg[1] = 13` replaces one
- `len(kg)`, `sum(kg)`, `max(kg)`, `min(kg)`, `sorted(kg)` (new sorted list), `kg.sort()` (sorts in place)
- `40 in kg` checks if it's there

Looping over a list with `for` is the most common thing you'll do in programming. When you need the position too, `for i, value in enumerate(kg):` gives both.

Building a new list from an old one: start empty and append, or use a **list comprehension**, a one-line loop: `big = [k for k in kg if k > 20]`, `doubled = [k * 2 for k in kg]`.

example.code:
kg = [40, 12, 55]
kg.append(30)
print(kg, len(kg), sum(kg), max(kg))
print(sorted(kg), kg)
for i, k in enumerate(kg, start=1):
    print(f"day {i}: {k} kg")
big = [k for k in kg if k >= 30]
print(big)
notes: sorted gives a new list; kg is unchanged.

exercises.title: Average harvest
exercises.prompt: Write average(nums): the average of a list of numbers, rounded to 1 decimal. An empty list gives 0.

tests.hint_if_fail: Dividing by len([]) is dividing by zero: check for an empty list first.

hints: Check if not nums: return 0 first, then round(..., 1).

exercises.title: Above average
exercises.prompt: Write above_average(nums): a new list with only the numbers bigger than the average, in the same order.
hints: Work out the average once, before the loop (watch for an empty list).
[n for n in nums if n > avg]

exercises.title: Biggest without max
exercises.prompt: Write biggest(nums) WITHOUT using max(): loop through and keep the biggest seen so far. Return None for an empty list. (This is how max works inside.)

tests.hint_if_fail: Starting the 'best so far' at 0 breaks for all-negative lists: start with nums[0].

tests.check: assert 'max(' not in CODE, 'Do it without max()'
tests.name: no max()

hints: best = nums[0], then for n in nums: if n > best: best = n
